_comment: Languages whose native script is non-Latin, checked by check_no_latin_leak in text_checks.py for stray Latin content (untranslated leftovers) outside the one known-good exception: the Latin transliteration inside a Greek/Hebrew gloss's parenthetical, e.g. 'μονογενής (monogenēs)' — see find_greek_hebrew_glosses. 'letters': flag bare Latin letters (A-Z/a-z plus accented Latin) found in the field. 'punctuation': flag ASCII punctuation (, . ! ? " ') where the language has its own native marks — OFF by default until confirmed against real corpus usage per language (this corpus intentionally tolerates some mixed punctuation conventions, see check_quote_anomalies comments on guillemets/curly quotes). Add a language only after confirming its script is genuinely non-Latin and the rule values are correct for it.
_skip_keys_comment: Field keys (matched by last JSON path segment, e.g. 'metadata.difficulty_level' matches 'difficulty_level') that are structural/identifier values by schema design, not translatable prose — legitimately Latin/ASCII regardless of language. Verified exhaustively: every value under every one of these keys, across all 53 zh files in discovery/zh + encounters/zh, contains zero Han characters (script-content check, not a guess from a sample). Add a key here only after confirming — the same way, corpus-wide — that its value is a schema identifier/code, not human-readable content.
_allowed_words_comment: Case-insensitive bare-Latin words that are content, not translation leftovers, in a specific language. Add an entry only after confirming the word is deliberately cited, not a missed translation. '×' (multiplication sign, U+00D7) is listed here: _LATIN_LETTER_RE's accented-Latin range (À-ɏ, U+00C0–U+024F) incidentally includes it since it sits inside that Unicode block by Unicode's own layout, not because it's a Latin letter — confirmed the identical U+00D7 codepoint is used as multiplication notation across ar/hi/ja/zh corpus content, not an untranslated leftover. No '÷' entry: the division sign does not appear anywhere in the corpus (confirmed via full-corpus scan) — add it back only if/when it's actually used.
